source.verbatim_statement: Let an acyclic mixed graph \(G\) be AC-identifiable and suppose that Assumption 7.1 holds. Then there is an identifying order \(\prec\) and a corresponding set of identifying polynomials \(P_{\prec}\) such that \(\max_{g\in P_{\prec}}\deg(g)\leq s^{4}+2s^{3}+s^{2}\).

proposed.comparator_claim: For prespecified \(d\geq ID_G\), the degree-bounded algorithm returns minimum-degree formulas; Propositions 7.2 and 7.3 bound half-trek and instrumental-cutset certificates by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\), and Proposition 7.4 bounds auxiliary-cutset certificates by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\).
A polynomial ideal generated in degree at most \(e\) in \(r\) variables has a Gröbner basis degree bounded by \(2(e^2/2+e)^{2^{r-1}}\).
The half-trek criterion is a polynomial-time sufficient criterion for rational identification by recursive linear systems.
Instrumental cutsets give a sound graphical identification criterion for linear structural causal models.
Auxiliary cutsets enlarge the efficiently certifiable subclass by recursively using identified coefficients as auxiliary information.
A missing cycle in a directed-tree model yields a quadratic equation, and multiple cycles can select one rational root.
Every directed-tree structural coefficient is generically one-identifiable, two-identifiable, or unidentifiable, and the classification is complete.
The complete tree-only identification predicate can be implemented in randomized \(O(n^3\log^2n)\) time.
A Cohen--Macaulay graph or Rees algebra yields inverse-degree bounds through regularity and Jacobian-dual minors.
Generic identification in unrestricted linear structural causal models has a sound and complete polynomial-space decision procedure.
Fixed half-trek estimators have recursive influence functions, asymptotic normality, and plug-in Wald inference.
Bow-free path recovery is stable under quantitative conditions, while a four-node example has unbounded condition number.
At a vanishing constraint gradient, the Wald statistic can converge to a nonstandard rational function of a Gaussian vector.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Decide whether the sequence \(D_2(n)\) is uniformly bounded; if so compute its sharp constant, and if not construct a dimension-feasible birational indegree-two family and prove a matching rate against all recursive structural and disturbance adjunctions.
open_obligations.obstruction: The former lower family is generically infinite-to-one and therefore cannot witness the published class. The effective Gröbner bound proves finiteness for each fixed graph size but is doubly exponential in an exponential and gives no information about whether the true supremum over sizes is finite.
open_obligations.attempted: The old windmill was rejected by its exact parameter-dimension excess. The six-vertex two-triangle system was instead solved exactly, and the cubic graph ideal was combined with effective lexicographic elimination. These routes give a constant lower witness and a total upper schedule but do not decide the elbow.

prose_updates.tldr: The exact two-triangle calculation gives \(ID_{K_6}=7\): closures at degrees one through six stop at \(\omega_{11}\), while degree seven identifies the shared chain coefficient and then every structural and disturbance coordinate. This puts \(K_6\) outside auxiliary-cutset identification and gives \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for \(n\geq6\) by isolated padding. Independently, the cubic graph-ideal presentation and Dubé's theorem give the unconditional effective bound \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\), which is compiled into the stopping-schedule definition. The sharp remaining question is the full-class elbow: whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite, and otherwise its rate. The old two-parent windmills remain only as a proved overparameterized counterexample. Fixed-chart inference is map-local and does not mathematically depend on how a deterministic rational map was found.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's algorithm is complete only relative to a supplied degree, and their half-trek, instrumental-cutset, and auxiliary-cutset bounds cover proper sufficient subclasses. The exact graph \(K_6\) now supplies an outside-auxiliary-cutset degree-seven witness, but no theorem decides whether \(D_2(n)\) is uniformly bounded on the full rationally identifiable indegree-two class or determines its sharp growth otherwise.
project_justification.niche: Directed indegree two is the first sparse class in which missing covariance equations can couple several structural coefficients while recursive orders may also exploit disturbance coordinates. The exact \(K_6\) closure demonstrates a genuine degree-seven obstruction beyond auxiliary cutsets, and the remaining niche is to decide whether such obstructions stay uniformly bounded or grow with graph size.
project_justification.fill: This round supplies an exact all-coordinate closure proof for \(K_6\), its outside-auxiliary-cutset consequence, isolated-vertex padding, and an unconditional effective elimination upper bound for the unchanged class \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{rat}}(n)\). The upper bound is compiled into an exact no-timeout stopping schedule. The headline frontier is honestly retained as the unresolved constant-versus-growth elbow, with every future lower family required to pass the parameter-dimension and birationality screens before criterion or degree audits.

prose_updates.related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and bound the half-trek and instrumental-cutset subclasses by \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) and the auxiliary-cutset subclass by \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\). Their \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}=1\) auxiliary bound turns the proved equality \(ID_{K_6}=7\) into a certified outside-auxiliary-cutset witness. Van der Zander et al. supply the missing-cycle algebraic architecture, while Gupta and Bläser and Briefs and Bläser concern the tree-only identification classification; the exact recursive degree-seven obstruction here is the additional conclusion. Dubé's classical Gröbner-basis degree theorem supplies only the crude effective upper bound, not the sharp elbow. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton, Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim, and Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim remain the graphical-criterion background. Dörfler et al. remain the total decision benchmark without the present degree compilation. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton are retained only as adjacent inference work: the fixed-chart argument here applies to any fixed deterministic rational map and is not derived from their estimator class.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact result \(ID_{K_6}=7\) is a constant lower witness, not evidence of growth with cycle length. The family \(W_{\ell}^{(2)}\) is inadmissible because it is generically infinite-to-one. The unconditional bound \(U_2(n)=2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\) is an effective elimination bound and is intentionally far too large to settle whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite. No dimension-feasible birational growing family or matching sharp upper argument is currently proved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved structural results are the all-order closure characterization, the exact small-size values through three vertices, the windmill nonidentifiability obstruction, the exact equality \(ID_{K_6}=7\) including all disturbance-coordinate shortcuts, the padded lower bound \(D_2(n)\geq7\) for \(n\geq6\), and the unconditional effective upper bound \(D_2(n)\leq2\cdot8^{2^{n(n+1)}}\). These results provide a total exact cutoff but do not determine the sharp full-class elbow. The inference result is fixed-dimensional and regular-chart, applies to any fixed deterministic rational identification map, and makes no efficiency, adaptive-selection, growing-dimension, or singular-chart claim. The old two-parent windmills and their Hilbert-rank obstruction are not presented as an identifiable lower family.
